mainTopic: Repaying loans through gifts to the poor, כהנים, and לויים (death, wealth, and heirs), and a ברייתא about holding a לוי's מעשר
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of a homeowner who lends money to a poor person, a כהן, or a לוי, and is paid back by keeping their share of the gifts. First the גמרא shows the practical difference between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי אחאי: the case of poor כותים. A ברייתא teaches that if the poor man becomes rich, the arrangement ends and he keeps the money. The חכמים made a fix for death but not for wealth, because death is common and wealth is rare, and רב פפא quotes a folk saying that makes the same point. Next, רבי יוחנן explains that the lender can continue with the heirs only if they inherited land, not money. רבי יונתן and רבי יוחנן then argue over how much can be collected from a small plot, and the גמרא compares this to a case in אביי's court. Finally, a ברייתא about a ישראל holding a לוי's מעשר gets three explanations, from אביי, רב משרשיא, and רב אשי. רב אשי's reading stands, based on the view of אבא אלעזר בן גמלא, whose proof from a פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The practical difference: poor כותים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question of what difference there is between the two views: the case of poor כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in the case of poor כותים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this point: what is the practical difference between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי אחאי? The answer is a case where the only poor people around are poor כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that כותים are not real converts, so they cannot take the place of the poor man in the arrangement. רבי אחאי holds that they are converts, so the arrangement can continue with them. The two opinions sound alike, but here they lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them (a practical case where the two opinions disagree)
Samaritans; their status as real converts is debated

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
poor Samaritans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי בינייהו' asked just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי אחאי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case where the only poor people available are poor כותים, whose status as converts is debated.

steps.title: If the poor man became rich, the arrangement ends
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the poor borrower became wealthy, the lender can no longer set aside מעשר עני against the loan, and the borrower keeps the rest of the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the poor person became rich, the lender may not set aside tithes against him any more, and that person keeps what is in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from a ברייתא. If the poor borrower became rich, the lender cannot keep taking מעשר עני to pay off the loan, and the borrower keeps the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loan was made from the start with the understanding that it would be paid back only through מעשר עני. A rich man is not allowed to receive מעשר עני, so that way of paying back is gone. The borrower does not have to pay back the rest from his own pocket.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rich borrower now owes the money back in cash. The ברייתא says the opposite: he keeps it, because the loan was only ever meant to be paid back through מעשר עני.

phrases.english: If the poor person became wealthy –
he may not separate tithes based on him,
and that one acquires what is in his hand.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the borrower. He keeps whatever part of the loan has not yet been paid back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new case in the same arrangement: the poor man becoming wealthy instead of dying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the poor borrower becomes rich, the lender can no longer take מעשר עני against the loan, and the borrower keeps the remaining money.

steps.title: Why a fix for death but not for wealth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים made a תקנה when the poor man dies but made none when he becomes rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for the חכמים: what is different about death, that they made a תקנה, and what is different about wealth, that they did not make a תקנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out something that seems inconsistent. The חכמים made a fix so the deal could continue if the poor man died, but they made no fix if he became rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the original poor man can no longer receive מעשר עני. So it seems the חכמים should have treated both cases the same way. The גמרא wants to know why they did not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking why two similar cases are treated differently)

phrases.english: And the Sages, what is different about death
that they made an ordinance,
phrases.notes: This is the fix mentioned earlier: after the poor man dies, the lender may continue with other poor people.

phrases.english: and what is different about wealth
that they did not make an ordinance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, מַאי שְׁנָא לְמִיתָה דַּעֲבוּד תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 2 by comparing it with the ordinance for death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the חכמים made a תקנה for death but not for wealth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both death and wealth end the poor man's ability to receive מעשר עני, so they should be treated the same.

steps.title: Death is common, wealth is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים made fixes for common situations, and death is common while getting rich is rare.
steps.simpleTranslation: Death is common; wealth is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Death happens all the time, so the חכמים made a fix for it. Getting rich is rare, so they did not bother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים usually make a תקנה only for situations that happen often. Since a poor man suddenly becoming rich is unusual, they left that case under the basic rule of the deal, and the borrower keeps the money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern across ש״ס: the חכמים usually make a תקנה for situations that come up often, not for rare ones.

phrases.english: Death is common,
wealth is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how often they happen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death and wealth should be treated the same, since in both the poor man can no longer receive מעשר עני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים made a fix only for the common case (death), not for the rare case (wealth).

steps.title: רב פפא's folk saying about death and wealth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports the answer with a popular saying: believe news that your friend died, but do not believe news that he got rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: 'Your friend died? Believe it. He got rich? Do not believe it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא backs up the answer with a saying people used. Death is so common that you can believe a report of it, but getting rich is so rare that you should not believe a report of it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying adds no new law. It shows that everyday life matches the גמרא's reasoning: people already know that death happens often and sudden wealth does not.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים let the deal continue after the poor man's death because death is common. When he becomes rich, the deal simply ends and he keeps the money, because wealth is rare.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said,
This is what people say:
Your friend died – believe it,
he became rich – do not believe it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 4 with a popular saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A popular saying confirms that death is common and sudden wealth is rare.

steps.title: רבי: permission is needed from heirs who inherited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that after the borrower dies the lender needs permission, and brings a ברייתא where רבי says this means 'heirs who inherited.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he died, he must get permission,' and so on. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, 'Heirs who inherited.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה: if the כהן or לוי who borrowed dies, the lender needs the heirs' permission to keep going. A ברייתא quotes רבי, who says this applies to 'heirs who inherited.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is narrowing down when the arrangement can continue with the heirs. The wording 'heirs who inherited' sounds strange, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: If he died – he needs to obtain permission, etc.:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the borrower כהן or לוי. 'Etc.' points to the rest of the line: permission from the heirs.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
Heirs who inherited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permission is needed from 'heirs who inherited.'

steps.title: Aren't all heirs people who inherit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'heirs who inherited' adds, since every heir inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are there heirs who do not inherit?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי's wording. By definition an heir is someone who inherits, so 'heirs who inherited' seems to say nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about wording. If the phrase adds nothing, why did רבי say it? This pushes the גמרא to find a real meaning behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really...? (an expression of surprise)

phrases.english: And are there heirs
who do not inherit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי's statement in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every heir inherits, so the extra words seem to add nothing.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: heirs who inherited land, not money
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי means heirs who inherited land, from which debts can be collected, and not heirs who inherited money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: It means those who inherited land, and not those who inherited money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains רבי's words. The lender can continue the arrangement, with permission, only when the heirs inherited land. If they inherited only money, the lender has nothing to collect from, so the arrangement cannot continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender can collect a dead borrower's debt from land the heirs inherited, but not from money they inherited. So only heirs who got land are tied to the debt, and only with them can the lender keep collecting through the gifts, after getting their permission. If they got only money, the lender has nothing to collect from. This gives 'heirs who inherited' a real meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the simple reading and giving a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Heirs who inherited' means heirs who received land, which a lender can collect from. If the heirs received only money, the lender cannot continue collecting the debt through the gifts at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying heirs of money are not real heirs. They are heirs, but a debt cannot be collected from inherited money. So the lender has no claim against them, and asking their permission would not help him.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Those who inherited land,
and not those who inherited money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by giving רבי's wording a specific meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Heirs who inherited' seems to mean all heirs, which would make the phrase pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only heirs who inherited land, since a debt can be collected from inherited land but not from inherited money.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: collect only as much as the land is worth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן rules that the lender may collect only up to the value of the land the heirs inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: if the borrower left land the size of a needle, the lender collects a needle's worth. If he left land the size of an ax, the lender collects an ax's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the heirs must have inherited land (Step 8), רבי יונתן tells us how much the lender may still collect from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debt now rests on the land the heirs received. So according to רבי יונתן, the land also sets the limit: a tiny plot lets the lender collect only a tiny amount. A bigger plot lets him collect more.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a needle, meaning a tiny amount of land
The size of an ax, meaning a bigger amount of land
He collects (here, he keeps taking the gifts as repayment)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ מְלֹא מַחַט – גּוֹבֶה מְלֹא מַחַט.
phrases.english: If he left land the size of a needle, he collects a needle's worth.
phrases.notes: "He left" is the borrower who died. "He collects" is the lender, who keeps taking the gifts to pay off the loan.

phrases.english: If he left land the size of an ax, he collects an ax's worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's point that the heirs must have inherited land, and asks how much can be collected from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collection is limited to the value of the land the heirs inherited.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a tiny plot allows full collection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: even if the heirs inherited only a tiny plot, the lender may collect a large amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: even if he left land the size of a needle, the lender collects an ax's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the other side of the מחלוקת. As long as the heirs inherited any land at all, the lender may keep collecting beyond the land's value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the land does not set the limit. It only has to exist. Once the heirs inherited even a tiny piece of land, the whole debt can be collected.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this רבי יוחנן with רבי יונתן in Step 9. The names look alike, but they hold opposite views here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even if he left land the size of a needle,
he collects an ax's worth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רבי יונתן in the same מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any amount of inherited land lets the lender collect the full debt.

steps.title: Like the case of the small field in אביי's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares רבי יוחנן's view to a known case in אביי's court about a small plot of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like the incident of the small plot of land of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a real case decided by אביי to show that רבי יוחנן's idea works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story itself is not told here; it is only referred to by name. The idea is that in אביי's case the orphans had inherited only a small field. Even so, the creditor was able to keep collecting from it until the whole debt was paid. This matches רבי יוחנן: a small plot can still back a big debt.

keyTerms.meaning: Small one (here, a small plot of land)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונתן: collect only as much as the land is worth. רבי יוחנן: even a tiny plot lets the lender collect the whole debt, like the case in אביי's court.

phrases.english: And it is like the incident of the small plot of Abaye.
phrases.notes: This points to a well-known case decided in אביי's court; the story itself isn't spelled out here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's view with a practical case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that a small inherited plot allows collecting beyond its value.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the small field ruled on by אביי.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a ישראל holding a לוי's מעשר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the following. If a ישראל tells a לוי he holds some unspecified מעשר of his, we are not worried about תרומת מעשר. But if he says he holds a כור of מעשר, we are worried.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a ישראל said to a לוי, "I have מעשר of yours." We are not concerned about the תרומת מעשר in it. If he said, "I have a כור of מעשר of yours," we are concerned about the תרומת מעשר in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. Its wording is unclear, and the גמרא will explain it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two cases is whether the ישראל named an exact amount (a כור). Somehow, naming the amount creates a worry about תרומת מעשר. The ברייתא does not say why, which sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth of produce given to a לוי
The tenth of the לוי's מעשר that he must give to a כהן; it is forbidden to non-כהנים
A specific, large measure of produce
We are concerned / we take into account

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An Israelite who said to a Levite:
"There is tithe of yours in my hand,"
we are not concerned about the teruma of the tithe in it.
If he said, "There is a kor of tithe of yours in my hand,"
we are concerned about the teruma of the tithe in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a ישראל who holds a לוי's מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified amount of מעשר raises no worry about תרומת מעשר; a stated amount (a כור) does.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, since the reason for its distinction is unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא is actually talking about. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether an amount is named should not change whether the produce contains תרומת מעשר. So the גמרא needs to know what case the ברייתא has in mind for this distinction to make sense.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the ברייתא is describing, and why naming the amount matters.

steps.title: אביי: the ישראל paid for it, and the לוי may have used it as תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ישראל paid the לוי for the מעשר. If the amount was named, the לוי may have declared it תרומת מעשר for his produce elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: a ישראל said to a לוי, "I have מעשר of yours, and here is its value in money." We are not concerned that the לוי made it into תרומת מעשר for other produce. If he said, "I have a כור of מעשר of yours, and here is its value," we are concerned that the לוי made it into תרומת מעשר for other produce.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by filling in the case: the ישראל bought the מעשר from the לוי for money. The worry is whether the לוי, from a distance, declared this מעשר to be the תרומת מעשר for other מעשר he owns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לוי can declare one batch of מעשר to be the תרומת מעשר for other מעשר somewhere else. If he does not know how much the ישראל holds, he cannot do this, so there is nothing to worry about. If he knows it is exactly a כור, he could have used it this way, so the ישראל must worry that it is now תרומת מעשר, which belongs to a כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the ישראל paid for the מעשר. When the לוי knows the exact amount, he might have used it as תרומת מעשר for his other produce, so we must worry. When the amount is unknown, we need not.
steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that the ישראל forgot to separate תרומת מעשר. The worry is that the לוי himself, knowing the amount, may have declared this מעשר to be תרומת מעשר for produce he has elsewhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person's declaration can change the status of produce he is not even holding, as long as he knows how much there is.

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
An Israelite who said to a Levite
"There is tithe of yours in my hand, and here is its value,"
we are not concerned that perhaps he made it
teruma of the tithe for another place.
phrases.notes: "He" is the לוי. He might use this מעשר to cover the תרומת מעשר owed on his other produce.

phrases.aramaic: ״כּוֹר מַעֲשֵׂר יֵשׁ לְךָ בְּיָדִי, וְהֵילָךְ דָּמָיו״,
phrases.english: "There is a kor of tithe of yours in my hand, and here is its value,"
we are concerned that perhaps he made it
teruma of the tithe for another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by explaining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ישראל paid for the מעשר. If the לוי knew the amount, he may have declared it תרומת מעשר for his other produce. If he did not know the amount, he could not have done so.

steps.title: Would a לוי sell his מעשר and then still use it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: his explanation assumes the לוי took money for the מעשר and then still declared it תרומת מעשר, which would make him a wicked person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we really talking about wicked people, who take money for the מעשר and then turn it into תרומת מעשר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's explanation from Step 14. It says his reading only works if the לוי is acting dishonestly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's case, the ישראל already paid the לוי for the מעשר, so it no longer belongs to the לוי. If the לוי then declared that same produce to be תרומת מעשר for his other produce, he would be using something that is not his. A ברייתא would not build a rule around wicked people, so אביי's reading is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a challenge that sounds unreasonable)
they make it into, they turn it into

phrases.english: Is that to say we are dealing with wicked people,
who take money
phrases.notes: This is the money the ישראל paid for the מעשר in אביי's explanation.

phrases.english: and then turn it into תרומת מעשר?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's explanation in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the ישראל paid the לוי and the לוי then declared the produce תרומת מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the לוי has been paid, the produce is no longer his. Declaring it תרומת מעשר would be a wicked act, and a ברייתא does not set its rules around wicked people.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: the לוי's son is paid after his father's death
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא בריה דרב אידי rereads the ברייתא: the ישראל pays the son of the לוי for מעשר owed to the late father. If a כור was named, perhaps the father had already made it תרומת מעשר for produce he had elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב משרשיא son of רב אידי said that this is what the ברייתא means. Suppose a ישראל says to the son of a לוי: "There is מעשר of your father's in my hand, here is its money." We do not worry that the father made it into תרומת מעשר for produce in another place. But if he says: "There is a כור of מעשר of your father's in my hand, and here is its money," we do worry that the father made it into תרומת מעשר for produce in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: Because אביי's reading was rejected, רב משרשיא offers a new way to understand the ברייתא. In his case, the father made the declaration before any money changed hands, so nobody is acting wickedly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment now happens after the father died, and it goes to his son. If the father knew the exact amount, a כור, he could have declared it תרומת מעשר while he was still alive. Then the son may not take money for it as if it were plain מעשר. If the amount was never named, the father could not have relied on it in that way.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who offers the second explanation
here is its money (payment in place of the produce)
another place, meaning other produce stored elsewhere
a large, fixed measure of produce

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי,
phrases.english: Rather, רב משרשיא son of רב אידי said,
this is what it is saying:
A ישראל who said to the son of a לוי:
"There is מעשר of your father's in my hand,
here is its money,"
we are not concerned that perhaps his father made it
into תרומת מעשר for another place.
"There is a כור of מעשר of your father's in my hand,
and here is its money,"
we are concerned that perhaps his father made it
into תרומת מעשר for another place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected reading with a new case that avoids the problem of a wicked לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the payment goes to the son after the father's death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes a לוי who was paid and then declared the produce תרומת מעשר, which would make him wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father declared it תרומת מעשר while alive, before any payment, so nobody acted wrongly. The only question is whether the son may now accept money for it.

steps.title: Careful people do not separate from produce that is far away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב משרשיא: a careful person would not separate תרומת מעשר from produce that is not near the produce it is meant to cover.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are חברים suspected of separating תרומה from produce that is not nearby?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב משרשיא's explanation. His case only works if the father separated תרומת מעשר from produce in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that when you separate תרומה from one batch to cover another, the two batches should be near each other (מוקף). The father's מעשר was sitting in the ישראל's house, far from the father's other produce. A careful, trustworthy person (a חבר) would not break this rule, so we have no reason to worry that he did.

keyTerms.meaning: people known to be careful about תרומות and מעשרות
nearby; produce right next to the produce being covered

phrases.english: But are חברים suspected
of separating תרומה from produce that is not nearby?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי נֶחְשְׁדוּ חֲבֵרִים לִתְרוֹם שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמּוּקָּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב משרשיא's explanation in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's worry that the father made the מעשר into תרומת מעשר for produce elsewhere.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That would mean separating from produce that is not nearby (שלא מן המוקף). We do not suspect a careful person of doing this, so the worry has no basis.

steps.title: רב אשי: did the owner already take off the תרומת מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the worry is whether the ישראל owner already separated the תרומת מעשר from the מעשר. If a fixed amount, a כור, was named, he surely did. If no amount was named, he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said that this is what the ברייתא means. Suppose the son of a ישראל says to a לוי: "This is what my father told me: 'There is מעשר of yours in my hand,'" or "'There is מעשר of your father's in my hand.'" Then we worry about the תרומת מעשר that is in it. Since no fixed amount was set, the owner would not have prepared it for him. But if he says "There is a כור of מעשר of yours in my hand" or "There is a כור of מעשר of your father's in my hand," we do not worry about the תרומת מעשר in it. Since a fixed amount was set, the owner surely prepared it.
steps.whatsHappening: After two explanations were rejected, רב אשי gives a third reading that avoids both problems. The question is no longer whether the לוי used the produce. Now the question is whether the owner already took the תרומת מעשר off it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner set aside an exact amount, like a כור, he treated it as a finished portion ready to hand over. So we assume he also separated the תרומת מעשר from it. When the amount was never fixed, he never got it ready, so the לוי who receives it must separate the תרומת מעשר himself. In רב אשי's case the speaker is the owner's son reporting what his father said, and the מעשר may belong to the לוי or to the לוי's father.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who gives the final explanation
prepares produce by separating what must be taken off
the owner of the produce (here, the ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading of the ברייתא (רב אשי): if a fixed amount of מעשר was named (a כור), we assume the owner already separated its תרומת מעשר. If no amount was named, we assume he did not, and it must still be separated.
steps.confusionAlert: Careful: the word 'worry' (חוששין) now means something different. Before, the worry was that the father turned the מעשר into תרומת מעשר. In רב אשי's reading, the worry is that the תרומת מעשר inside the מעשר was never taken off. That is why his 'worried' and 'not worried' land on the opposite cases from רב משרשיא's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the explanation that stands: Step 19 challenges it and Step 20 defends it. It shows that naming a fixed amount marks the מעשר as a ready, prepared portion.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said, this is what it is saying:
The son of a ישראל who said to a לוי:
"This is what my father told me:
'There is מעשר of yours in my hand'"
or "'There is מעשר of your father's in my hand'" —
we are concerned about the תרומת מעשר that is in it,
since it was not a fixed amount,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה מְתַקֵּן לֵיהּ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: the owner would not have prepared it for him.
"There is a כור of מעשר of yours in my hand"
or "There is a כור of מעשר of your father's in my hand" —
we are not concerned about the תרומת מעשר that is in it,
since it was a fixed amount,
the owner surely prepared it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב משרשיא's rejected reading with a new explanation that avoids both earlier problems.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the worry is about: whether the owner already separated the תרומת מעשר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was that the לוי or his father had turned the מעשר into תרומת מעשר for other produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is whether the owner already separated the תרומת מעשר. A fixed amount (a כור) shows he prepared it. An unfixed amount shows he did not.

steps.title: Can the owner separate תרומת מעשר at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: the בעל הבית has no right to separate תרומת מעשר, because that belongs to the לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does the owner of the produce even have permission to separate תרומת מעשר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's explanation. It asks how the owner could separate תרומת מעשר when that is the לוי's task.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer assumed the ישראל owner took off the תרומת מעשר before handing over the מעשר. But תרומת מעשר is taken by the לוי from the מעשר he receives, so the owner seems to have no standing to separate it. If the owner cannot do this, רב אשי's explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner, here the ישראל who owns the produce
To separate a portion as תרומה
The tenth of the מעשר that is given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two separations. The owner gives מעשר to the לוי, and then normally the לוי takes תרומת מעשר out of it for the כהן. The question is whether the owner can do that second step himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: And does the homeowner have permission
to separate the תרומה of the tithe?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת לִתְרוֹם תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption at the heart of רב אשי's answer in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the ישראל owner may have already separated the תרומת מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת מעשר is the לוי's job, so the owner seemingly has no authority to separate it. That would undercut רב אשי's whole explanation.

steps.title: Yes, this follows אבא אלעזר בן גמלא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the owner can separate it, because the ברייתא follows the opinion of אבא אלעזר בן גמלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The ברייתא follows אבא אלעזר בן גמלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by saying yes, the owner can separate it. It points to a תנא who holds this view, אבא אלעזר בן גמלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not claim everyone agrees. It says this ברייתא was taught according to one specific opinion that allows the owner to separate תרומת מעשר. That is enough to save רב אשי's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinion is about to be quoted

phrases.aramaic: אִין, אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גַּמְלָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Yes, it is the opinion of Abba Elazar ben Gamla.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גַּמְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the לוי can separate תרומת מעשר, so the owner could not have done it.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אבא אלעזר בן גמלא the owner may separate תרומת מעשר, and the ברייתא follows him.

steps.title: The source for אבא אלעזר בן גמלא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא in which אבא אלעזר בן גמלא cites a פסוק about תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: אבא אלעזר בן גמלא says: "And your תרומה shall be reckoned to you".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof. It begins quoting where אבא אלעזר בן גמלא states his view, starting with the פסוק he learns it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about the לוי's תרומת מעשר, using the word תרומתכם, "your תרומה." The rest of his explanation, showing how this lets the owner separate it, continues on the next amud. For now, notice that the proof is built on this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
And it shall be reckoned for you

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גַּמְלָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Abba Elazar ben Gamla says:
"And your gift that you set apart shall be reckoned to you"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:27. His explanation of the פסוק comes right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גַּמְלָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the attribution in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That according to אבא אלעזר בן גמלא the owner may separate תרומת מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting אבא אלעזר בן גמלא's reading of במדבר 18:27, "ונחשב לכם תרומתכם".
